segments.normalizedSource: ```swift /// Extract the name, email address, and phone number from a table into a list of contacts. private func parseTable(_ table: DocumentObservation.Container.Table) -> [Contact] { var contacts = [Contact]() // Iterate over each row in the table. for row in table.rows { // Take the contact name from the first column. guard let firstCell = row.first else { continue } // Extract the text content from the transcript. let name = firstCell.content.text.transcript // Look for email addresses and phone numbers in the remaining cells. var detectedPhone: String? = nil var detectedEmail: String? = nil for cell in row.dropFirst() { // Get all detected data in the cell, then match emails and phone numbers to a contact. for data in cell.content.text.detectedData { switch data.match.details { case .emailAddress(let email): detectedEmail = email.emailAddress case .phoneNumber(let phoneNumber): detectedPhone = phoneNumber.phoneNumber default: break } } } // Create a contact if an email was detected. if let email = detectedEmail { let contact = Contact(name: name, email: email, phoneNumber: detectedPhone) contacts.append(contact) } } return contacts } ```

segments.normalizedSource: ```swift /// Convert the table into a TSV string format that's compatible with pasting into Notes or Numbers. /// /// Tables have at most one line per cell, and no cells that span multiple rows or columns. func exportTable() async throws -> String { guard let rows = self.table?.rows else { throw AppError.noTable } // Map each row into a tab-delimited line. let tableRowData = rows.map { row in return row.map({ $0.content.text.transcript }).joined(separator: "\t") } // Create a multiline string with one row per line. return tableRowData.joined(separator: "\n") } ```
